validity.recommendation: Investigate merge of P1923 into P1922 (or confirm as a distinct parallel line). Treat as one Berri<->Abu Ali corridor split by diameter; do not retain P1923 as an independently-sourced entity without a source that names a second/10-inch line.
validity.researcher_notes: P1923 'Berri-Abu Ali 2' (Berri Gas Plant -> Abu Ali Island, len=39 km, dia=10 in, operating) is near-identical to P1922 'Berri-Abu Ali' (same endpoints, same 39 km length, dia=8 in). The pair is a classic parallel-line / diameter-split double-count of a single corridor. EXISTENCE of the Berri<->Abu Ali corridor is independently confirmed (Saipem 'Berri Downstream Pipeline' 2019-2023 describes Abu Ali Island <-> Khursaniyah/Juaymah lines, verified OK; NS Energy Berri Oil Field Expansion page, verified OK). However NO independent source distinguishes a SECOND, 10-inch gas line ('Berri-Abu Ali 2') from the 8-inch P1922 — every web result for the specific specs traces back to GEM pages. The row's ONLY citation on the gem.wiki page is 'OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, p.75', which is shared verbatim across the entire Saudi gas cluster (P1921, P1922, P1923, P7768 all cite the identical line) AND, when fetched and checked, the OPEC ASB 2012 PDF returns 200 but does NOT contain the string 'Berri' at all (FAIL on token 'Berri'). So the sole citation does not actually corroborate this pipeline; it is a generic statistics bulletin, not a pipeline-segment list. Net: the corridor is real, but P1923 as a discrete, independently-sourced gas pipeline distinct from P1922 is unverified. Flagging duplicate (vs P1922) as the primary concern.

validity.recommendation: Verify commodity: confirm whether the Berri<->Abu Ali 10-inch line carries dry gas vs sour condensate/NGL. Saipem's 10-inch Abu Ali line carries 'stabilized Arabian light crude oil and sour condensate', not dry gas.
validity.researcher_notes: Secondary concern: the only independent corridor descriptions (Saipem Berri Downstream Pipeline) describe the Abu Ali <-> Khursaniyah/Juaymah lines as carrying STABILIZED CRUDE OIL and SOUR CONDENSATE, and one of the two new lines is 10-inch (matching P1923's diameter). This raises doubt that the 10-inch Berri<->Abu Ali line is dry-gas transmission as recorded ('Fuel = Gas'). It may be a condensate/NGL or crude line, or a feeder tied to the Berri Increment Program rather than a dry-gas trunk line. Note the Saipem project is 2019-2023 while GEM records P1922/P1923 as long-operating with OPEC-2012 sourcing, so they may be older lines; cannot resolve commodity with confidence from available independent sources. Flagging for commodity/type verification.

summary: P1923 concern: likely duplicate/parallel-line split of P1922 (same endpoints, 39km, only diameter differs 8 vs 10); sole citation (OPEC ASB 2012 p.75) does not even contain 'Berri'; corridor existence confirmed independently (Saipem/NS Energy) but no source distinguishes a discrete 10-inch gas 'Berri-Abu Ali 2', and independent corridor sources describe crude/condensate not dry gas.
